Every field is labelled the way you would say it out loud, so you can usually fill the form from memory and only look up the numbers you genuinely do not know.

sections.title: How does the Social Media Time Alternatives calculator work?
sections.html:
The Social Media Time Alternatives calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports learning time in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the activity and the skill level); then you type in the time wasted, the reading duration per page, the you could read and the hourly wage.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Social Media Time Alternatives calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

I visit social media=time wasted ÷ I usually spend
Money earned=hourly wage × time wasted
Average page has=60 × time wasted × reading speed ÷ (you could read × average book has...)
MET=(1 ÷ 112) × energy burnt ÷ (time wasted × your weight)
Money earned=price tag on your dream ÷ you will get it in
Average page has=reading duration per page × reading speed

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Social Media Time Alternatives calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Testing how sensitive an answer is to one input
  • Checking a figure someone else quoted
  • Turning a rough idea into a number you can act on
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the time wasted, the reading duration per page and the you could read — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Social Media Time Alternatives calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns learning time, derived from the time wasted, the reading duration per page and the you could read. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Social Media Time Alternatives calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the time wasted, the reading duration per page, the you could read and the hourly wage, which is 11 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter I visit social media in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. I visit social media opens in hours and the chip beside it offers 7 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (2 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Time wasted = 630 hrs. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Social Media Time Alternatives calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
